summary: Round 5, scoped to the delta since 6e889cf0920b (a rewritten `rounds:M4.8b1`, the backlog-done clause recording the new case, and one assertion in LogKeysTest). The test-side change is correct and I measured it rather than read it: over a standalone replica of the staged LogKeys logic, `logPrefix() + "delta"` answers false on the unmutated record (endsWith('.delta') fails because logPrefix ends in '/'), and under `endsWith(SUFFIX)` narrowed to each of "delta", "elta", "lta", "ta", "a" it throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: Range [32, 31) out of bounds for length 37 -- exactly the figure the backlog row now quotes -- while keyFor(9) still returns true under every one of those mutants, so 'leaves every real key passing' and 'or to any suffix of it' are both true as written. The `.as()` text ('ends with a proper suffix of ".delta"') is accurate, and the case genuinely belongs to `aKeyTooSHORTToCarryTheGrammarIsRefusedRatherThanThrowing`: 37 < logPrefix.length() + SUFFIX.length() = 38. No production file changed this round, so the cost lens is unmoved: no get/put/list/stat is added, and the filter remains a pure string test over keys a LIST already returned. The backlog row's M4.23 correction, the ChainReplay paragraph's remaining clauses and the guard mutants I verified in round 4 and did not re-open. What I am blocking on is again the artifact this round rewrote. The old entry was blocked for misdating the first survivor and calling later rounds prose-only; the rewrite fixes exactly that and then makes a smaller instance of the same error in the same direction. `.harness/review` records FOUR successive rounds each measuring a new surviving mutant in `isEntryKey` -- round 1 the round trip (both roles), round 2 both length-guard deletions, round 3 the startsWith narrowing, round 4 the endsWith narrowing (test-reviewer T3, `endsWith(SUFFIX)` -> `endsWith("delta")`, 254 tests green under it) -- and the entry says three, stopping at the startsWith narrowing and omitting the one round 5 exists to carry, whose fix is the assertion in this very diff. Two minors below, neither blocking.

findings.title: The rewritten `rounds:M4.8b1` still undercounts, in the same flattering direction: four rounds each measured a new survivor in `isEntryKey`, and the one it omits is the one this diff fixes
findings.detail: The entry leads with 'THREE SUCCESSIVE ROUNDS EACH MEASURED A NEW SURVIVING MUTANT ON THE SAME TWELVE-LINE METHOD, and that is the fact worth carrying rather than the round total', enumerates the round trip, both length-guard deletions and 'the NARROWING of one of them to the bare prefix component', and closes 'Each fix's tests failed to reach the next gap, in the same method, three times.' Measured against the recorded verdicts, by mtime in .harness/review: fcf8d15b8ee8 (reviewer 10:53, test-reviewer 10:57) = round 1, round-trip mutant from both roles; 006aa9aad9dd (11:08, 11:10) = round 2, test-reviewer minor 'Two mutations survive the whole suite: deleting either half of the guard'; 19d8ae11daa3 (11:19, 11:20) = round 3, test-reviewer T2 '`!key.startsWith(logPrefix)` -> `!key.startsWith(prefix)` ... BUILD SUCCESSFUL'; 6e889cf0920b (11:30, 11:32) = round 4, test-reviewer T3 'SURVIVING MUTATION, measured against the full :sequencer:test (254 tests, all green): `key.endsWith(SUFFIX)` -> `key.endsWith("delta")`'. That is four rounds, four new survivors, all in the same twelve-line method, and the fourth is not mentioned anywhere in the entry -- neither in the enumeration nor in the count. The staged backlog-done row records it ('a fourth, `<logPrefix>delta`, pins the suffix guard's ... measured') and the staged LogKeysTest now carries the assertion that kills it, so the entry disagrees with two other documents in the same commit, which is the precise defect the entry's own third clause says it was rewritten to remove. Two further internal contradictions come with it: the entry asserts 'NO COUNT IS GIVEN, deliberately: a number here is stale the moment the verdict it describes is recorded' while its lead sentence gives a count, and that count went stale one round before it was written -- the failure mode it cites M4.8b for. The cheapest fix is the entry's own stated remedy, applied to itself: name the four mutants and drop the numeral, e.g. '... then the narrowing of the startsWith guard to the bare prefix component, then the narrowing of the endsWith guard to a proper suffix of ".delta", each new gap missed by the cases the previous fix added.' No code, test or measurement changes.
findings.failure_scenario: A later session reads `rounds:M4.8b1` to judge what exceeding the cap bought and what the recurring failure was. It is told the fix-then-miss cycle ran three times and ended at the startsWith narrowing, so it takes the last round as the verification round the cap describes. .harness/review and this commit's own backlog row and test file all record a fourth: `endsWith(SUFFIX)` -> `endsWith("delta")` survived the whole 254-test suite while making `<logPrefix>delta` throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException Range [32, 31) out of `chainEnd`/`applyChain` -- the takeover-loop failure this task exists to remove. Under review.md rule `two-round-cap` this line is the only trace in the tree of why rounds 3-5 happened, so an account that stops one round short suppresses the newest finding while looking like disclosure, and it is the second time the same entry has understated its own history in the direction that flatters the change.

findings.title: New clause in the entry: 'every seeded interloper died one step earlier in `Long.parseUnsignedLong`' is true of one of the three interlopers, not all
findings.detail: ChainReplayNonDeltaKeyTest seeds three foreign keys: `<logPrefix>ckpt/<seq:016x>.ckpt`, `<logPrefix>0000000000000001.delta.tmp` and `<logPrefix>ckpt/<seq:016x>.delta`. Only the third reaches `Long.parseUnsignedLong` (its digits are `ckpt/...`); the first two end in `.ckpt` and `.tmp` and are refused one guard earlier still, by `endsWith(SUFFIX)`. The point the clause is making survives -- every interloper died before the round trip, which is why `return true` left the suite green -- but the named guard is wrong for two of the three, and the same over-generalisation already sits in the backlog row and in LogKeysTest's class javadoc (both pre-existing and already carrying verdicts, so only the new copy is in scope here). 'died at an earlier guard, one of them at `Long.parseUnsignedLong`' is the accurate form. Under `minors-land` this lands; fixing it is permitted and, given this task's history, the fix is the next round's surface.
findings.failure_scenario: A later session reasoning about which guard is doing the work reads that the parse alone refused every interloper the end-to-end file seeds, concludes the two length guards and `endsWith(SUFFIX)` are only reachable through hypothetical keys, and weakens or removes one -- when in fact `endsWith(SUFFIX)` is what refuses two of the three keys that test seeds today.

findings.title: 'every round returned findings against the TESTS ... or against my prose' is refuted by the entry's own next sentence, and by a round-1 production finding it never mentions
findings.detail: The opening claim 'No round returned a finding against what `isEntryKey` decides' is TRUE -- I checked all eight recorded verdicts and no finding faults the predicate's answers. The clause after it is not: round 1 returned two findings against production code rather than against tests or prose. One is the dead `CommitLog.isEntryKey` delegate, which the entry names two sentences later, contradicting the clause it just made. The other it never mentions at all: round-1 reviewer finding 3's second half recorded that swapping `new CommitLog(store, prefix, epoch)` for a bare `LogKeys` at `chainEnd` and `applyChain` silently drops the constructor's null-prefix and negative-epoch guards (`LogKeys` is a bare record and `String.format` renders a null prefix as the literal 'null' and epoch -1 as `ffffffffffffffff`, which sorts above every real epoch). That finding is unreachable through today's callers and was correctly left unfixed, but it is a finding about the staged production code, and the entry's taxonomy has no room for it. Narrowing the clause -- 'every round's other findings were against the tests or the prose, plus two against new production surface in round 1' -- costs one clause.
findings.failure_scenario: A later session reads the entry as an inventory of what review found on this task and never learns that the LogKeys substitution at the two listing sites dropped the argument validation `CommitLog`'s constructor performed. When a caller reaching `chainEnd`/`applyChain` with a computed epoch appears (M4.23's walk, M5's forwarding), the loss shows up as a well-formed key at `ffffffffffffffff` that sorts above every real epoch rather than as an IllegalArgumentException, and the record that flagged it lives only in a gitignored directory.
